deviations: Knesset website unreachable: main.knesset.gov.il and www.knesset.gov.il answer with 'The site is temporarily inaccessible from your location' (maintenance-page-geo), and fs.knesset.gov.il returns a 303 to that page; the Knesset's own government, law and bill pages could therefore not be read. Government composition was taken from the English Wikipedia articles on the 26th, 27th, 28th, 29th and 30th governments, as the sheet permits when the Knesset site is unreachable.

Knesset plenum records: the sittings for all twelve vote dates were identified from the Knesset's plenum-session table as mirrored by Open Knesset (production.oknesset.org/pipelines/data/plenum/kns_plenumsession and kns_documentplenumsession), which give each sitting's record file on fs.knesset.gov.il. Only the record of 31 July 2000 (15_ptm_532783.docx) has an Internet Archive capture; the other thirteen files (13_ptm_532430, 532443, 532423; 14_ptm_532483, 532538, 532706; 15_ptm_532918, 532838, 532938, 533062, 533006, 533067; 16_ptm_129138) have none (CDX index empty under both URL spellings). Archived pages of the Knesset's older Tql record system were also checked: only two items from 26 and 28 February 1996 exist, neither covering a Basic Law vote, and the 346 archived mark01 items contain nothing from the batch's dates. Tallies for seq 39, 42, 45, 48, 51, 54, 64, 67 and 70 are therefore not found; coalition_only is blank for those and for seq 58 (tally known, names not recorded).

Internet Archive was intermittently offline ('Temporarily Offline' pages) during the work, and several captures could be retrieved only by addressing a specific timestamp because the latest captures of fs.knesset.gov.il are the geo-block redirect.

Seq 67: the sheet's PDF link (15_lsr_300419) is Basic Law: The Knesset (Amendment No. 34), not the President amendment named in the row. The President amendment (Basic Law: The President of the State (Amendment No. 6)) was found at 15_lsr_300418 (archived 2016-03-04): same bill (ה״ח 3027), same passage date (16.10.2001), same gazette page (ס״ח 1809 p. 2). Both are coded as one row per the instruction that each row is the whole law as passed, with the note that they are two separately titled laws; a third ordinary law from the same bill (15_lsr_300420) was opened only to identify it.

Seq 39 and 45: the sheet gives only the Nevo consolidated text; the gazette PDFs were located by scanning the archived 13th Knesset law series (13_lsr_211270 for seq 39, 13_lsr_211244 for seq 45) and used for the text and bill dates. Neighbouring PDFs (13_lsr_211240–211243, 211251–211252, 211271–211278) were opened only to identify them. Seq 54 and 61: gazette PDFs not located; Nevo consolidated text with its amendment markers used.

First-reading dates were found for none of the twelve enactments (Knesset bill pages unreachable; records unarchived). Where the bill's publication date in הצעות חוק lies within thirty days before the final vote (seq 42, 45, 51, 58, 64, 73), expedited is coded Yes on the ground that the first reading cannot precede the bill's publication; elsewhere it is blank.

Seq 54: the MFA page quoting the Jerusalem Post of 5.1.1999 (embassies.gov.il and mfa.gov.il) reset the connection on every attempt (ECONNRESET x3; curl returned a 3 KB stub); its content (85–27–1 for the dissolution law, Netanyahu absent) is known only from the web-search summary and from the Jewish Virtual Library's Fourteenth Knesset highlights page, which gives the date but no tally. It concerns the dissolution law, not this amendment.

Seq 61: the tally rests on the Jewish Virtual Library's page 'Knesset Passes Netanyahu Bill, But Doesn't Dissolve Itself', which quotes the Jerusalem Post of 19.12.2000; the newspaper itself was not reached.
Open Knesset's law tables (kns_law, kns_israel_law, kns_document_law) were downloaded but contain no rows for these enactments; they were not used.

Hebrew Wikisource pages for Basic Law: The Knesset, Freedom of Occupation, The Judiciary and The President were read for section texts and amendment lists; the page for the 1992 Government law does not exist (404), so Nevo was used for that law.

No court judgment, summary of a judgment or page about litigation was opened; no page had to be closed for that reason. Explanatory notes were reachable for none of the enactments; named_beneficiary is coded from the enacted texts alone.
